narration_timeline.text: Why does this small European robin keep singing from such an exposed perch?
narration_timeline.scene: European robin audibly or visibly singing from reeds.

narration_timeline.text: That small bird uses a clear song to announce its presence across nearby habitat.
narration_timeline.scene: European robin on an ordinary perch in a Ljubljana park.

narration_timeline.text: One robin sings from deep in the reeds while another gives short notes from a completely different perch.
narration_timeline.scene: Two independently filmed European robin singing sequences.

narration_timeline.text: A repeated song can help a robin signal its territory to other robins.
narration_timeline.scene: Real European robin in park habitat; territorial meaning is narration, not a filmed dispute.

narration_timeline.text: But between vocal moments, the same species must also spend time looking for food.
narration_timeline.scene: Genuine European robin feeding, not footage of a different robin species.

narration_timeline.text: The song is more than background noise: it is a clear message carried through the surrounding trees.
narration_timeline.scene: Two further authentic European robin perches or movements, without invented singing behavior.
